correctness.rationale: Spherical invariance gives an exact Beta(1/2,(n−1)/2) weight. One-node Lanczos and degree-one endpoint interpolation reduce to explicit rational functions of that weight; the interpolant risk is the scaled beta variance. Absolutely convergent moment generating series produce exact risk-gap coefficients and recurrence; the recurrence is strictly negative for n≥4. Dimension 2 has a closed radical risk ratio >1; dimension 3 has coefficient signs switching once, proving exactly one risk crossover, with the opposite near-singular sign from dominated convergence. Standalone exact rational and numerical checks passed 18,835 assertions. No finite tests are used as proofs of the universal statements.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the exact non-asymptotic risk ordering, dimension-four uniform domination, and unique three-dimensional reversal. Existing work provides underlying stochastic quadrature constructions, general high-probability errors and Gauss/interpolation definitions, but not a statement implying this mean-square ordering in the inspected matching settings. A pointwise Jensen inequality is strictly weaker: it cannot settle MSE relative to the target and yields opposite outcomes in different dimensions. Semantic database and literature searches were compared by objects and implications, not title alone; residual priority uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: Both compared one-matvec estimators arise naturally in stochastic spectral quadrature, and the exact theorem explains a genuine finite-budget risk reversal between an unbiased polynomial and a biased one-node Gauss rule. It distinguishes three sharp dimension regimes and yields an exact critical condition number in dimension three; these give a precise benchmark for bias-variance and algorithmic test cases. Limited to a prescribed rank-one two-level spectrum with exact baseline endpoints, not advertised as a general or practically dominant estimator.
